featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Newly opened restaurant with another branch in Goregaon east.

The interiors are beautifully done, with Marathi songs playing in the background, adds to the authentic vibe. A special mention to Abhishek Prabhu, the manager, who was extremely helpful and guided us through the menu.

We were welcomed with papads served alongside three sides – thecha, green chutney, and masala oil – all packed with flavour.

The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was a highlight: steamed in green masala and then finished in a banana leaf. The fish was fresh and tasted amazing, especially when paired with the masala oil.

We also tried the Mutton Kolhapuri Thali, which came with pandra rassa, tambda rassa, kheema, and Kolhapuri gravy, along with bhakri, masala bhaat, and salad. A hearty and satisfying meal.

Although we initially skipped dessert, Abhishek insisted we try their freshly made in-house ice creams in jackfruit, guava, and coconut jaggery flavours — and they were absolutely out of this world! To our surprise, he didn’t even charge us for them despite our insistence.

We paid around ₹2000 for two people. It’s slightly on the higher side, but the food, service, and overall experience made it worth it. Definitely visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text: Something or the other is always missing from their menu... Would love to be able to order any dish... Hence the 4... Else the food and service and atmosphere is awesome! Crisp fried fish awesome thalis... The crabs that could be deshelled slightly... Especially if they are the big ones with the hard shell or they are very difficult to enjoy to the fullest which is a shame because they are absolutely finger licking good... Been there twice already looking forward to going there many more times.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very good spot for authentic Maharashtrian-style mutton thali in Bombay. Good job with the interiors and music,  beautifully capture Maharashtra’s culture

While it’s still not quite at the level of the iconic thalis in Pune, it’s definitely a great start for Bombay. The mutton quality was good and the portions are huge — almost too huge. Looking forward to going back and trying more dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Vivian Nguyen
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Marathi friend recommended me to come here and oh my… it was insanity. I already came in not hungry, but I cleared everything. After the meal, even though I was so full, I was still missing the taste of the meal I just had. On my walk back, I could taste the breath of the best meal I’ve ever had in India (& I’ve had a lot of dishes) I didn’t want to brush my teeth so I could savor the taste (but I did brush my teeth)

When I arrived, the owner told me (not verbatim), “Apologies for the smoke, because of the gas shortage, we are using coal fire to cook.” It’s a terrible situation, for sure; a lot of restaurants have been suffering from the gas shortage… but I guiltily admit I was even more excited to try the food because nothing elevates a dish more than the taste a coal brings.

The ice cream was next level, too. All made in house, real fruit, no preservatives. Left to right: coconut jaggery, guava, custard apple, and they were all amazing.

A lot of times in India, restaurants/accommodations will ask me to write a good review for them. This is 100% an organic review, unprompted. I just needed to tell the world how good this mutton thali was!!

The service was kind, attentive, and exceptional on top of everything out. I’m flying out of India on Sunday, and I am already grieving the loss of access to one of the most delicious meals I’ve ever eaten.

featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing seafood experience at Gajalee! featured_reviews.name: Yogesh Karnik
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most popular seafood restaurants in Vile Parle East, Mumbai. On weekends and public holidays, waiting time is expected and can range from 30 minutes to an hour, so make sure to register your name at the counter while you wait.

The ambience is warm and welcoming, and the service is good, though delays are common during peak hours—so it’s best to place your order in one go. The food is undoubtedly excellent: portions may be on the smaller side, but the quality is top-notch. Prices are on the higher side, with most dishes around ₹500 and desserts priced at about ₹220.

Thalis are sometimes unavailable (as happened during our visit), which meant ordering individual dishes and stretching the budget a bit. The variety of seafood on offer is fantastic—a true paradise for seafood lovers. Don’t miss the Solkadhi; it’s absolutely authentic. Desserts are optional and up to your preference. Enjoy your food...

featured_reviews.review_text: If you love seafood and you are in Mumbai then it’s an absolutely must visit. I’ve been to Gajalee twice, first time in 2015 and 2nd time in 2026 and there’s no change in taste. The food is absolutely delicious and freshly prepared. We enjoyed everything we ordered and almost licked the plates clean 😁. You are missing out on something good if you miss visiting places when in Mumbai. The servers, the on ground manager all warm, helping and courteous. They keep checking on you if you need anything and promptly serve food and remove empty plates. Overall Gajalee has my heart ❤️ and is on my must visit place every time I am in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Nisikant Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gajalee recently for seafood, and the experience was mixed. While the restaurant has a strong reputation and offers a wide variety of seafood (including crab, pomfret, oysters, and even snails), the pricing feels significantly inflated for what is essentially a standard dining setup.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.
N.B: After having Pomfret, I have been suffering from stomach upset (Food poisoning) and currently recovering.

featured_reviews.review_text:
In a very long time, I wasn’t filled with such a subtle and home-blend restaurant. Calling it a restaurant might be over exaggerating because this place is run by a family and the authentic Goan food that they serve just makes you feel at home. This charming place is nestled right beside the highway, amidst a small colony of homes. It’s seamlessly blended in, creating an atmosphere that feels more like a family’s home than a resting place.
We have got the Surmai Fish Curry Thali and the classic Chicken Masala Thali. Both were just amazing and homely to taste.

Their staffs are very friendly and sweet enough that you feel like home.

While the quantity of food didn’t quite match the pricing, the quality was great.

This is very good place to recommend for a family lunch/dinner. I am sure you won’t be disappointed with it. Enjoy.

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Mukul Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Got to know about this place via Google as I was in BKC and wanted to eat fish, looking at the rating I thought of visiting this place.
The place is quite small and gives homely feeling, looking at this i got happy thinking the food would be really nice and homemade.
We ordered for a chicken thali, a pomfret thali and an surmai thali and a tisrya sukkah.
Was totally disappointed when the food came, the tisrya sukkha seemed like tisrya masala and was very sweet. The surmai thali was not upto the mark, surmai was very small, I have never had such small piece of surmai in any of the fish outlet.
Quantity wise I was totally disappointed, chicken thali had just 2 pieces of chicken.
Sol kadhi seemed to be like water added to it, we had reached around 2:30-2:45pm and I think we were served the left over food as it was closing time.
I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone, specially who is a fish lover.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Amrute
featured_reviews.review_text:
In Mumbai, people are often misguided into thinking Mangalorean or Goan Cuisine as Malvani.. But not here…!!

So I came here today with a friend. He ordered a Tisrya (Clams) Thali and I called for Mori (Shark) Thali. Both were excellent. The fish was fresh and the gravy was very tasty and perfectly spiced. The quantity in each thali was perfect for one adult. If at all I have to complain then I would say, I missed the small portion of Suka Jawla (dry baby shrimp) that is also served as part of the seafood thali in my town.

The service was prompt and the staff was welcoming. Hygiene is taken care of. The place is tiny and very modestly done up, so if you value the ambience as much as your food, then this isn't the place for you. Free Street Parking is available.

If you are craving for good authentic Malvani Food… Sadichha is just the place for you.

featured_reviews.review_text: What a find this place. It's located just opp the MIG club...it's a quaint tiny lil place..serving seafood like a boss! We ordered everything and lived everything. The bombil fry, prawns, mandeli, the pomfret stuffed with prawns (awesomeness) and all the thalis..we had prawn, mory, clams, surmai and pomfret thalis..and for vegetarians with us they specially made some pithala and a good veg thali :). featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.name: Nataleigh Lasrado
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Fresh Catch on 4 June 2026 and it was excellent!  I asked the bartender to create me a great custom drink and he exceeded my expectations with refreshing and unique creations. featured_reviews.name: Chanjeet Dhawan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

Regards!
CSD

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

What truly sets Jai Jawan apart is its consistency and authenticity. The masalas are aromatic without being overpowering, allowing the seafood to remain the star of the show.

The service is quick, efficient, and warm, adding to the overall comfort of the dining experience. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, dig in, and leave completely content.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). featured_reviews.name: Hania
featured_reviews.review_text:
Peach Ice Tea
Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Amritsari Kulcha
The Amritsari-styled kulcha is a delightful treat. Each bite offers a perfect blend of crispy exterior and soft, flavorful interior. The traditional stuffing of spiced potatoes and herbs is well-seasoned, providing a hearty and satisfying taste

Lachha Paratha
The Lachha Paratha is a standout with its perfectly layered, crispy texture. Each bite reveals a delightful combination of flaky. Though they forgot to add butter because it was some miscommunication, It was perfect size not big not small.

Tadkewali Dal
Tadkewali Dal delivers a heartwarming, flavorful experience. The smoky aroma from the tadka (tempering) hits you immediately, preparing your senses for a rich and comforting dish. The lentils are cooked to perfection—and well-spiced. The tadka of ghee, cumin, garlic, and chilies adds depth, bringing a savory warmth to every bite. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of velvety dal and robust, fragrant spices. It’s a perfect dish for anyone seeking bold yet balanced flavors in a simple, soul-satisfying homely meal.

Jeera rice
Jeera Rice is simplicity at its finest. The delicate aroma of cumin wafts through each grain, giving the rice a warm, earthy fragrance. The cumin seeds add a subtle crunch and a toasted, nutty flavor that complements the perfectly cooked, fluffy rice.

Halwa (Complementary)
Rich and buttery, each spoonful melts in your mouth, releasing a wave of sweetness that’s perfectly balanced with hints of cardamom. The texture is smooth yet slightly grainy, with bursts of flavor from the roasted nuts scattered throughout.

Hospitality
The hospitality at this restaurant is exceptional. From the moment we walked in, the staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming. They ensured every detail was taken care of, making us feel comfortable and valued throughout the meal. Service was prompt, yet never rushed, with the team showing genuine care in their recommendations and interactions. Their professionalism, combined with friendly smiles, truly elevated our experience. Ashish and Prasad served great hospitality to us.

Ambience
The ambience of Rasoi strikes the perfect balance between luxury and comfort. The decor is elegant yet welcoming, with soft lighting and tasteful accents that create a warm, inviting atmosphere

Nom Nom is such a vibe!

The ambience really stands out! That warm, dim lighting sets the perfect mood for an intimate dinner without feeling too “try-hard.” It’s the kind of place where you naturally slow down, settle in, and actually enjoy the evening.
The food, overall, was really good and definitely amps up the experience. That said, I’d love to see a wider variety of sushi and noodle dishes on the menu. The bao bun was a bit on the chewy side, and the filling-to-bun ratio felt slightly off (could’ve used more filling). The silken tofu, though was an absolute standout. It genuinely melted in the mouth and was a wow dish, even if I wish the portion was a little more generous. The peach iced tea was perfect. Dessert-wise, the mango sticky rice could’ve been better, it felt a bit like mango purée with pieces and rice, missing that coconut-y flavour and crunch (both of which are not very difficult to crack).
Definitely a spot I’d come back to (and happily recommend) when I’m in the mood for a relaxed, date-night style dinner.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.name: Suhani Mendonsa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar just got a delicious new reason to celebrate with Bawa Kitchen opening its doors this Lohri! From the first bite, it felt like a true Punjabi feast — rich, soulful and full of festive warmth. My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!
And yes, my festive Lohri fit was specially curated — can’t wait to share it with you all soon!

featured_reviews.review_text:

The food quality was nice, especially the North Indian dishes which were flavorful and well-prepared. Portion sizes were decent and prices felt reasonable for the location.

featured_reviews.name: Jawahar Hingorani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I only gave 4 for atmosphere because there was no 4.5 or 4.75…and I got bitten by mosquitoes! The food was on point - I ordered Ajwaini Rawas for my appetizer and it came with this spicy tandoori salad (think Thai Som Yum but not as sweet or wet) and Green chutney which was the perfect accompaniment. For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Vijita Sonawane

Special mention to Rahul for being an excellent host—his food suggestions and positive approach added real value to the experience. Overall, a visit that is absolutely worth it for good food, warm hospitality, and Punjabi flair.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambience & Parking: ⭐⭐⭐

Service: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Excellent. The staff was incredibly quick, efficient, and responsive throughout the meal.

Food & Drinks:
✅ Truffle Salmon Sushi - Absolute perfection with amazing flavor. (5/5)
✅ Egg Fried Rice - Flawless, classic taste, and good portion size. (5/5)
✅ Avocado Cream Cheese Sushi - A great, creamy option. (4/5)
✅ Chicken and Chilli Oil Dumplings - Nice flavor with a good spicy kick. (4/5)

❌ Lemon Ice Tea & Jade Mojito - Both felt a bit uninspiring for the price. (3/5)
⭐Truffle Salmon Sushi - Easily the standout dish of the entire meal!

Pricing & Value:
Our bill was around ₹4,500 for 3 people. Given the good portion sizes and quality of the mains, it felt fair.

💡Pro Tip:
Pre-book on Zomato! They have a 25% discount running, but slots are limited.

Overall:
A solid spot with remarkably fast service and excellent sushi, though it's held back slightly by average drinks and stiff seating.

Would I Recommend It?
Depends (Definitely go if you can grab the Zomato discount and stick to their top-tier sushi).

Must Try:
Truffle Salmon Sushi, Egg Fried Rice

Skip:
Chicken Spring Roll, Jade Mojito

featured_reviews.name: chanakya dhiman
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Unforgettable Asian Dining Experience in the Heart of Khar!
If you're looking for a restaurant that delivers on every front — breathtaking interiors, extraordinary food, and an experience that lingers long after the meal — look no further than PF Chang's, Khar. This place is an absolute gem, and my recent visit left me completely blown away.

The moment you step inside PF Chang's, you're transported into a world of stunning elegance. The interiors are nothing short of spectacular — a seamless blend of contemporary design and rich Asian-inspired aesthetics. From the dramatic lighting and intricate décor to the beautifully curated artwork and warm, inviting tones, every corner of this restaurant is Instagram-worthy. The space feels luxurious yet comfortable, making it perfect for a romantic date night, a family celebration, or a fun outing with friends. It's the kind of place where the ambiance alone is worth the visit.

Now, let's talk about the food — because PF Chang's truly takes Asian cuisine to another level. The menu is a love letter to the flavors of Asia, and every dish we tried was an absolute revelation. The dishes were bursting with bold, authentic flavors, perfectly balanced with the right amount of spice, sweetness, and umami. The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the presentation was exquisite. From the starters to the mains, each plate was crafted with care and culinary finesse. This is Asian food at its absolute finest!

The staff were warm, professional, and genuinely passionate about making your dining experience special. The team was attentive without being intrusive, and their knowledge of the menu made ordering an enjoyable experience in itself.
Overall, PF Chang's in Khar, Mumbai is a world-class dining destination that truly lives up to its global reputation. It's not just a meal — it's an experience. If you haven't visited yet, you're seriously missing out. This is one restaurant I will be returning to again and again without hesitation.
Highly recommended — a perfect 10/10! 🥢✨

featured_reviews.name: Mohak Khullar
featured_reviews.review_text: Mumbai has really good chinese food, so the bar was high. But sadly PF chang's didn't fully live up to it. The dynamite shrimp was the best part of my meal. If you are thinking of coming here I would recommend you to eat the starters only and skip the dynamite broccoli.

featured_reviews.name: Ninad joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Whenever I intended to travel to Mumbai, we always make an effort to discover new dining; this time, we chose to visit P.F. Chang's in Khar.

On Saturday evening, our cousins planned to go to this venue, so we made a reservation through Zomato.

After we settled in, one of my cousins started placing the order. We enjoyed the following dishes:
- Orange Chicken
- Original Dynamite Shrimp
- Avocado Cream Cheese Roll
- Aburi Salmon Roll
- Handmade Chicken Dumplings
- Pan-Fried Crab Wonton
- Wok Charred Chicken
- Hand-Folded Crab Wontons
- Signature Lo Mein
- Singapore Street Noodles
- Sticky Toffee Pudding
- Chicken in Black Bean Sauce
- Hot Garlic Sichuan Chicken

**Must Try**
1. Orange Chicken; this dish was exceptionally delicious, and the flavor of the orange was outstanding.
2. The Original Dynamite Shrimp was delightful in taste, featuring a blend of creamy, spicy mayonnaise, sriracha, and sweet chili sauce.
3. The Handmade Chicken Dumplings were also quite tasty.

**Recommendation**
Both sushi rolls were delicious, and I would recommend them:
1. Avocado Cream Cheese Roll
2. Aburi Salmon Roll

The service was prompt, and the highlight was that every dish arrived on time. The soothing background music contributed to a relaxing atmosphere.

Overall, it was a wonderful experience for us, and I would certainly recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: Roosa and Gigi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I absolutely loved dining at Mahesh! The seafood, especially the lobster and crab, was incredibly fresh and flavorful. You can really tell the quality of the ingredients in every bite.
The prices are also very reasonable considering the freshness and taste of the food, which makes the experience even more worth it.
The tables are a bit closely spaced, but it actually adds to the cozy, homey atmosphere, almost like dining with family or among friends.
Overall, it was a great experience, and I will definitely be coming back to try more from their menu.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

featured_reviews.name: Eda Basaran
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dined here this evening based on several recommendations. While the quality of the main course (butter chicken & rice & Wok fried crab) was very good and clearly reflects the skill of the kitchen team, the overall experience was unfortunately impacted by poor service.

The staff appeared inattentive, and one item, which is one of the signatures recommended by the staff ( king prawn) was served incorrectly / extremely cold which was disappointing. Basic service standards and attention to detail were lacking throughout the visit.

With improved staff training and better guest engagement, this restaurant has strong potential, as the food itself is commendable. I hope to see improvements in service on future visits.

featured_reviews.name: Al J
featured_reviews.review_text: We had an delicious family dinner at Mahesh Lunch Home, a seafood gem in the Mumbai Juhu district. The pomfret fish, prepared in two fantastic styles, was perfectly spiced with just the right kick of heat, paired beautifully with fluffy rice, buttery soft naan, and creamy daal. The shrimp curry stole the show—rich, flavorful, and ideal for sharing. The friendly staff tailored recommendations to our tastes, making it family-friendly for sharing. We capped off the spicy feast with a smooth caramel custard pudding. Highly recommend!
